title: Linkability of Student Identity to Submission Data
description: The flow transmits student id, course, and submission timestamp alongside the work file, enabling potential linking of the student's identity to their academic submission data.
assumptions: The system stores and processes this data in a way that allows correlation between identity and submission content.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for linkability concerns in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Identification of Student Through Login Credentials
description: The student must authenticate to submit assignments, which inherently identifies them to the system and potentially to other system components.
assumptions: Authentication credentials are processed and stored by the Grades Portal Web App.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard identification threat node for authentication scenarios.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Submission Data
description: The work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: The Grades Portal Web App may have inadequate access controls or security measures.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node for data flow scenarios.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity for Assignment Submission
description: An unauthorized actor could potentially submit assignments on behalf of the student, either through credential theft or system manipulation.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential compromise or session hijacking.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard usurpation threat node for authentication and submission scenarios.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This flow contains unique references to student identity that could be exposed during transmission or at the receiving process.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats; confidence in exact node mapping is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This processing of personally identifiable information creates privacy risks if access controls are inadequate.
assumptions: P2 processes the received identifying data for grading purposes without sufficient access restrictions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 from context describes processing of identified data; applies to P2 as the receiving process.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Submissions
description: The flow involves grading requests and file submissions where students or instructors may need to deny or confirm their involvement. Without proper audit trails, parties may be unable to deny claims about their submissions or grading actions.
assumptions: The system lacks sufficient audit logging or cryptographic evidence to support non-repudiation of grading-related actions.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation threat type Nr applies; specific tree node Nr.1.1 inferred from context §Nr — Non-repudiation description.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via Assignment Storage
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores assignment files containing student identifiers, course information, and submission timestamps. This creates a data disclosure risk where personal data is transferred to the Assignment Store, potentially exposing student information to unauthorized access or unintended third parties.
assumptions: The stored data may be accessible beyond intended recipients; student identifiers link submissions to individuals
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a reasonable fit for data disclosure in Process→DataStore flows based on context [5]

title: Linkability of Assignment Data to Student Identity
description: Assignment files stored with student IDs enable linking of submission data to specific students, potentially allowing correlation with other data sources (e.g., grades, course enrollment, behavioral patterns).
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers that can be used to link data across systems
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability threats

title: Identifiability of Student Submissions
description: The stored assignment data includes student IDs and course information, making submissions directly identifiable to specific students. This identifiability persists even if the assignment content is anonymized.
assumptions: Student IDs are not pseudonymized or hashed before storage
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats

title: Data Integrity Risk for Stored Assignments
description: Assignment files stored in the Assignment Store could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted, affecting the integrity of academic records and potentially leading to unfair grading outcomes.
assumptions: No adequate access controls or integrity checks are in place for the Assignment Store
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data integrity threats

title: Processing of identified student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that may contain personally identifiable information (e.g., student names, IDs, or other identifiers). This processing could potentially link submissions to specific students, creating identifiability risks.
assumptions: Student submission data contains or can be linked to PII
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 from context as it directly addresses processing of identified data

title: Unauthorized disclosure of submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose student submission data to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leaks, or insecure transmission channels.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient or data transmission may be insecure
uncertainty_note: Standard threat for data processing flows

title: Teacher account usurpation
description: An attacker may usurp a teacher's account to access submission data they should not have access to, potentially viewing submissions from courses they don't teach or accessing data of other teachers' students.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to account takeover
uncertainty_note: Standard threat for authentication flows

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student personal information (names, work content, submission times) displayed to teacher could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties if teacher credentials are compromised or data is shared inappropriately
assumptions: Teacher has access to student data and may share it with others

title: Unauthorized access to student submission data
description: Student data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals if teacher credentials are compromised, shared, or if the portal lacks proper access controls
assumptions: Teacher account security is not foolproof

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: Teacher could potentially link student submission data with other data sources to create comprehensive student profiles beyond intended scope
assumptions: Teacher has access to multiple data sources

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance in student data sharing
description: Sharing student personal information may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other privacy regulations if proper consent, data minimization, and safeguards are not in place
assumptions: Institution may not have proper consent mechanisms or data handling policies

title: Student Data Linkability Across Flows
description: Student identifiers recorded in this flow (student id) could be linked to other student data flows within the system, enabling correlation of student activities across different educational processes.
assumptions: System contains multiple data flows involving student identifiers

title: Student and Teacher Identification
description: The student id and grader id fields in this flow directly identify individuals. Student privacy is at risk as their academic records are tied to their identity, and teacher identity is exposed through grader id.
assumptions: Student and teacher identities are not anonymized in the system

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grades and Feedback
description: Grades and written feedback recorded in this flow could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, unauthorized personnel) through improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced

title: Teacher Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the teacher (EE3) to record grades and feedback, compromising the integrity of the grading process and potentially harming students.
assumptions: Teacher authentication may not be sufficiently robust

title: Student Identifiability in Grade Records
description: Grade records contain student IDs that directly identify students, enabling identification of individuals from the database.
assumptions: Student IDs are included in the grade records and are not anonymized.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Information
description: Grade records containing student performance data, feedback, and grader information could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Access controls on the Grade Records Database may be insufficient or bypassed.

title: Linkability Across Educational Systems
description: Grade records with student IDs, courses, and timestamps can be linked with other educational data sources to create comprehensive student profiles.
assumptions: Other systems may share student identifiers or course information.

title: Grader Identity Usurpation
description: Grader IDs in grade records could be compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to appear as legitimate graders or manipulate grading records.
assumptions: Grader authentication mechanisms may be weak or bypassed.

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Grade records containing sensitive student information may not comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: Data handling procedures may not fully align with applicable privacy regulations.

title: Processing of identified student grade data
description: The system processes identified student data (grades and feedback) which contains personal information that could be used to identify the student. This processing occurs when the student requests their own grades through the web app.
assumptions: The grades and feedback are linked to the student's identity in the system

title: Linkability of student grades to identity
description: Grades and feedback data could be linked to the student's identity through the web app interface, potentially enabling unauthorized correlation of academic performance with personal information.
assumptions: The system maintains records linking grades to student identity

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the web app, improper access controls, or data leakage during transmission.
assumptions: The web app has access controls that may not be fully enforced

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) displays sensitive student grades and teacher feedback to the Student (EE1). If access controls are inadequate, unauthorized parties could intercept or access this data through network vulnerabilities, session hijacking, or improper authentication mechanisms.
assumptions: The portal has network exposure and authentication mechanisms that could be compromised.

title: Linkability of Student Grades to Identity
description: Student grades displayed by the portal could be linked to the student's identity or other personal data, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other datasets. This linkability risk exists if the portal does not properly anonymize or separate grade data from identifying information.
assumptions: Grade data contains or can be correlated with student identifiers.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak, an attacker could impersonate a student and access another student's grades and teacher feedback. This usurpation risk arises from inadequate identity verification in the portal's access control system.
assumptions: The portal relies on authentication that could be bypassed or compromised.

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent by compromising their login credentials, gaining unauthorized access to another parent's child grades.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the system lacks proper access controls or if data is transmitted insecurely.
assumptions: Inadequate access control or insecure data transmission

title: Parent-Child Identity Linking
description: The system could link parent identity to child grades in ways that create privacy risks, such as revealing which parent accesses which child's information.
assumptions: System logs or metadata could expose linking relationships

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The Grades Portal Web App may collect more personal data than necessary for the grade request function, such as unnecessary parent or child demographic information.
assumptions: System collects data beyond what's needed for grade access

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Academic Data
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history displayed to the parent could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, insecure transmission, or improper access controls. This includes potential exposure to other family members, school staff without authorization, or external attackers.
assumptions: Assumes the portal has access controls and the data is transmitted securely, but these may be insufficient.

title: Linkability of Academic Data to Child Profile
description: The parent could link the displayed grades and feedback data to other personal information about the child (e.g., medical records, behavioral data, or other school records), creating a comprehensive profile that could be misused.
assumptions: Assumes the parent has access to other data sources that could be linked with this information.

title: Unauthorized Access by Non-Parent Individuals
description: Individuals other than the authorized parent (e.g., siblings, extended family, or others with access to the parent's credentials) could access the child's grades and feedback through account sharing, weak authentication, or social engineering.
assumptions: Assumes the parent may share credentials or the authentication system is not sufficiently robust.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: The handling of children's academic data may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA in the US, GDPR in Europe) if data is disclosed without proper consent, retained beyond necessary periods, or shared with unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the system operates under jurisdictions with data protection regulations and that the portal's data handling practices may not fully comply.

title: Identifiability of Personal Information in Account Management
description: Administrator creates/modifies accounts containing names, emails, and parent-child relationships that directly identify individuals. This personal data is processed and stored in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Administrator has access to enter and modify personally identifiable information

title: Linkability of Account Data Across Systems
description: Account information (names, emails, relationships) created by administrator could be linked to other data sources or systems, potentially enabling cross-referencing of student/parent identities across different platforms.
assumptions: Data may be shared or accessible across multiple systems
uncertainty_note: Depends on system integration and data sharing policies

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account and Relationship Data
description: Administrator has privileged access to create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links. Improper access controls could lead to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal information including names, emails, and family relationships.
assumptions: Administrator access is not properly restricted or monitored

title: Usurpation of Administrator Privileges
description: An unauthorized actor could potentially impersonate the School Administrator to gain access to account management functions, leading to unauthorized creation or modification of accounts and relationships.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised or insufficient

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Administrative Actions
description: Administrative actions (creating, modifying, disabling accounts) may not be properly logged or audited, allowing administrators to deny performing certain actions or making unauthorized changes.
assumptions: Audit logging may be incomplete or not enforced

title: Linkability of Account Records Across Systems
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. These relationships could be used to link student records across different educational systems or contexts, potentially revealing family connections that should remain private.
assumptions: The account directory is accessible to multiple systems that could correlate parent-child data

title: Identification of Students and Family Members
description: Account records with parent-child relationship links written by the grading service could be used to identify individual students and their family members, potentially exposing sensitive family structure information.
assumptions: The account directory contains sufficient identifying information to link records to specific individuals

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory. If the directory is not properly secured, unauthorized parties could access sensitive student and family information including parent-child relationships.
assumptions: The account directory may have insufficient access controls or encryption

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory. Without proper access controls and audit logging, unauthorized actors could modify account records or parent-child relationship links, leading to data integrity issues.
assumptions: The account directory may lack proper write access controls and audit mechanisms

title: Regulatory Compliance Concerns for Family Data
description: Parent-child relationship data written by the grading service may be subject to special regulatory protections (e.g., FERPA, GDPR). Improper handling could result in compliance violations.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is considered sensitive personal information under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Third-party provider has access to all PII; data transfer is intentional and by design

title: Identifiability of Students via Grade Records and Account Directory
description: Grade records and account directory contain personally identifiable information that can identify individual students/users. Transfer to third-party increases identifiability risk.
assumptions: Grade records and account directory contain sufficient PII to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Personal Data Across Systems
description: Account directory and grade records can be linked to identify individuals and potentially correlate with other data sources held by the cloud provider or third parties.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to other data sources; account directory enables cross-referencing

title: Data Integrity During Transfer to Cloud Hosting
description: Full database backup transferred to external provider may be subject to tampering, corruption, or unauthorized modification during transit or storage.
assumptions: Data in transit or at rest could be modified by unauthorized actors

title: Usurpation of Data by Third-Party Provider
description: Cloud hosting provider EE5 may misuse, repurpose, or share the transferred personal data beyond the intended scope of the hosting agreement.
assumptions: Third-party may have incentives to exploit data; contractual safeguards may be insufficient

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Third-Party Data Transfer
description: Transfer of student grade records and account directory to external cloud provider may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other educational privacy regulations if proper safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations require strict controls on third-party data transfers

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized parties or systems without proper authentication and authorization controls, exposing sensitive student performance data.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced on the grade records database.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for DataStore origin.

title: Student Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students, potentially leading to privacy violations if accessed inappropriately.
assumptions: Grade records include student identifiers or can be correlated with other data to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identification threat node for DataStore origin.

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (e.g., demographic, behavioral) to create comprehensive profiles, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Grade records can be correlated with other data sources to create linked profiles.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node for DataStore origin.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Sensitive Data
description: Grade records may contain sensitive personal data subject to privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR), and improper handling could result in regulatory violations and legal consequences.
assumptions: Grade records are classified as sensitive personal data under applicable privacy regulations.
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a representative non-compliance threat node for DataStore origin.
